title: Applied Geometric Modeling of an Inscribed Rectangle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A rectangle is inscribed under the parabola y = 9 - x^2 such that its base rests along the x-axis and its upper two vertices touch the parabola. Express the area A(x) of the rectangle as a function of the positive x-coordinate of its right vertex, and state the natural physical domain of A(x).
hints: Use symmetry: if the right vertex on the x-axis has coordinate (x, 0), the left vertex is at (-x, 0), giving a total base width of 2x.
The height of the rectangle is given by the y-value of the parabola at that coordinate: y = 9 - x^2.
Formulate the area as width multiplied by height, and require both dimensions to be strictly positive for a non-degenerate geometric figure.

steps.title: Determine Rectangle Dimensions from Coordinates
steps.explanation: Because the parabola y = 9 - x^2 is symmetric across the y-axis, placing the right vertex at x implies the left vertex is at -x. The distance between them is x - (-x) = 2x, and the vertical height is y = 9 - x^2.
steps.why: Even functions possess y-axis symmetry, guaranteeing that geometric inscriptions symmetric about the axis have horizontal width 2x.

steps.title: Formulate the Area Function
steps.explanation: Multiply width by height to obtain the polynomial formula for area: A(x) = 2x(9 - x^2) = 18x - 2x^3.
steps.why: The geometric area of a rectangle is the product of its base length and height.

steps.title: Establish the Physical Domain Restrictions
steps.explanation: For a physically realizable rectangle with positive area, both the width (2x > 0 ==> x > 0) and the height (9 - x^2 > 0 ==> x^2 < 9 ==> x < 3) must be strictly positive.
steps.why: Physical models restrict mathematical domains to intervals where lengths and areas remain strictly positive.

steps.title: State the Physical Domain in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: The allowable inputs for x are all real numbers in the open interval (0, 3). At the endpoints x = 0 and x = 3, the rectangle collapses to zero area (degenerate).
steps.why: Open intervals exclude the degenerate boundary cases where width or height vanishes.
